english.title: Carry / remove / deposit / harbour / keep / conceal a drug of Class C from a warehouse to evade a prohibition - Khat

english.legislation: Contrary to section 170(1)(b), (3) and (4) of and Schedule 1 to the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
knowingly concerned in
carrying / removing / depositing / harbouring / keeping / concealing / dealing with
khat which had unlawfully been removed from a warehouse / King's warehouse
with intent to evade a prohibition / restriction on the importation / exportation

investigatoraction.description: Criminal lifestyle offence under Schedule 2 to POCA - consider confiscation order
Submit a form Crimsec 38 where drugs are seized
Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Any goods in respect of which an offence under this section is committed shall be liable to forfeiture.
(ii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale or of three times the value of the goods whichever is the greater.
Indictment: Fourteen years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Twenty years
